rapport_notes: Warm greeting and friendly closing, but several stumbles during data entry (name/email spelling) and explanations created minor friction; generally professional but not exceptionally smooth.
process_discipline_notes: On-Time Guarantee mentioned twice — first in Stage 1 as part of the rate explanation ('our or guarantee which obviously if we don't arrive in the timeslot...') and mentioned again as part of the rate summary, representing a repeat of a differentiator.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'So let me go ahead and at least create this profile so I can make sure you're set up there' and jumps to logistics questions without a clear time-box or framing trade (no 'this should take X minutes, then we'll get you a quote' structure).
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep launches directly into address, square footage, items, and move details without any open-ended discovery of Isabella's concerns or priorities beyond the online quote.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No concerns raised by customer = no follow-up opportunity. Rubric grants N/A/full credit per explicit exception (item #3).
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Covered in Stage 1 as part of rate explanation: 'we have the network damage coverage that does cover-up. To $2,000 worth of incidentals.'
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Covered in Stage 1 as part of rate summary: 'a few days before the move, you'll receive an email introducing you to the movers, so all of the Ed is included.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Covered in Stage 1: 'we have the...our or guarantee which obviously if we don't arrive in the timeslot that we scheduled, the money is automatically deducted off of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.communication: Covered in Stage 1: 'a few days before the move, you'll receive an email introducing you to the movers.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: 'generally for this square footage usually it'll take us...we estimate generally about $6 and a half to $8 and a half...I would get this at about six to seven hours' and then personalized to move: 'your message that you have, you just have fifteen boxes...the estimate that it gave you online, I mean, cause I would get this at about six to seven hours.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: 'again an estimate, and then if we end up going shorter than that, then that's all you'll end up paying for but it'll be fine and then obviously that depends on how well prepared everything is.'
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Customer raised concern about overpaying if move finishes in 2 hours but charged for 6. Rep clarified: 'No, that, that's okay. No, no, no, no, it's there that has nothing to do with, with them...if we do [need it longer]...if it takes less time that's all you pay for anyway.'
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or held silence after an open-ended question. Moved directly to next logistics probe.

top_strength: Chauntelle successfully delivered the four core differentiators (On-Time Guarantee, damage coverage, Meet Your Mover email intro, and transparency on pay-for-time-used) organically within Stage 1, giving the customer a complete value story without waiting for Stage 2.
coaching_note: Skip the quid pro quo framing and their-agenda discovery entirely; you moved straight to logistics questions without earning trust or understanding Isabella's actual priorities—add the agenda line before any probing, and if she raises a concern, follow up twice (two layers deep) instead of one question and pivot.
